price_per_million.source: copied from reasoning_models_v1 (confirmed 2026-11-11); thinking tokens billed as output

research_concepts: shaper role (assumed comparable to the connector role in prior work; not confirmed)
role portability after a team change
methodological_questions: How are 'travel' and portability defined, and is the definition independent of the cut/drive profile label?
Can n=24 units detect the effect sizes seen in earlier work?
Are cut-heavy and drive-heavy labels derived from pre-move data only, and are they compositional mirrors of each other?
How do mover selection, regression to the mean and destination context confound the comparison?
Is 'shaper' the same population as the 'connector' in prior work?

historical_evidence.finding: Among 92 connector movers, pre-move cut share predicted whether the organizational function reproduced after a move (rho=+0.265, p=0.011, AUC 0.653). Cut minus drive gave rho=+0.314, p=0.002. Drive share gave rho=-0.278, p=0.007. The top cut tercile was 65% portable versus 35% in the bottom tercile. Leave-one-out AUC was 0.622 and the permutation p was 0.005. The record lists LIM:small_sample and RISK:SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER.

The connector diet x destination gap-match test had connector subsets of only n=19/40 (n=5/14 matched vs mismatched). The connector delta p was 0.156 and the all-movers binary result (p=0.0283) did not replicate as a continuous Spearman. The record lists the question as not answerable with the design and limited by small sample.

With n=44, the minimum detectable effect at 80% power was about 0.18 PPP (SD~0.34). The observed gap was below the minimum detectable effect, so a true null could not be distinguished from a moderate effect.
Destination net-rating checks for movers were recorded as underpowered and null once corrected for landing-spot quality. No numbers were given, and the check was dropped from Paper 1.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Subgroup tests of connectors (n=19/40) and an all-movers binary test used as a proxy for the connector test
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as small sample and unanswerable. The all-movers significance did not replicate as a continuous association and was not the licensed connector test.

failed_approaches.what_failed: A null-ish comparison at n=44 with outcome measured in PPP
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as low power with a large minimum detectable effect (0.18 PPP), so the null was uninformative.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using destination net rating change as the outcome for movers
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as underpowered, and null after correcting for landing-spot quality.

evidence_establishes: For connector movers (n=92), the earlier family recorded a supported positive association between pre-move cut share and portability, and a negative one for drive share, with a permutation p of 0.005 (FAM:SF-CHT-057).
Earlier project attempts at small-sample mover subgroup tests (n of about 19 to 44) were recorded as untestable or underpowered (FAM:SF-APPS-090, FAM:SF-APPS-024, FAM:SF-PAP-029).
evidence_does_not_establish: That the connector result transfers to 'shapers', if shapers are a different or narrower population than connectors.
That the effect is detectable at n=24. The records give no power calculation for this unit count.
That the result is causal or free of destination-context confounding. Only net-rating checks that were corrected for landing-spot quality are recorded, and those were null and underpowered.
Whether FAM:SF-CHT-057 had an out-of-sample replication. Only leave-one-out and permutation checks are recorded in the retrieved text.
own_inferences: The question as posed is close to a restatement of the FAM:SF-CHT-057 hypothesis, applied to a smaller unit set. This is a replication or extension, not a new question.

Assuming a true rho of about 0.27 to 0.31 (from FAM:SF-CHT-057), power at n=24 is roughly 20-25%. 80% power would need rho of about 0.55. A dichotomous cut-heavy vs drive-heavy comparison with about 12 per group is weaker still.
Cut share and drive share are likely partly mirrored (compositional), so the 'drive-heavy' comparison adds little independent evidence beyond the cut-minus-drive contrast.
The 92 connector movers probably include some or all of the n=24 shapers, so combining them would double-count evidence.
With n=24, a positive point estimate would be fragile to dropping one or two players. FAM:SF-CHT-057 itself needed drop-one and top-3 checks.
uncertainties: How 'shaper' is defined, and whether the 24 units are movers, player-seasons or team-seasons.
How 'portable' or 'travel' is operationalised here. The Delta metric in FAM:SF-CHT-057 is not described in the retrieved text.
Whether the cut/drive profile and the portability outcome share inputs (the same play-type records).
Whether 2025-26 movers are complete enough to serve as a holdout.
Overlap between the 24 units and earlier samples.

historical_effect.explanation: Without history, the question looks like a fresh test. The retrieved record shows a supported directional result at n=92, which makes a confirmatory, single-contrast replication worthwhile. The other records show small-n tests of similar movers ending untestable. So the decision is proceed_with_changes (one pre-registered contrast, framed as estimation and replication) rather than a free-standing confirmatory test, and a null at n=24 must not be read as rejection.

blocking_constraints.text: n=24 gives roughly 20-25% power for the previously observed rho of about 0.27 to 0.31. A null would be uninformative.
The cut/drive profile and the portability measure both derive from the same play-by-play and play-type records, so shared inputs could produce association without a real portability effect.

prior_work.summary: FAM:SF-CHT-057 recorded a supported cut-over-drive portability association for connector movers (n=92). Whether it applies to the 'shaper' subset of 24 is not established. Related small-sample mover tests were recorded as untestable.

risks.text: n=24 gives low power and unstable estimates. Any single player can swing the result.
Cut and drive shares and the portability outcome come from the same derived play-type records. Any shared inputs must be excluded or the outcome measured on independent possessions.
Cut share and drive share are partly compositional mirrors, so 'drive-heavy' is not independent of 'cut-heavy'. Thresholds on them create an arbitrary dichotomy.
The destination team's structural needs, coach, teammates and usage change alongside the move. Earlier net-rating checks were null once landing-spot quality was corrected (FAM:SF-PAP-029).
Movers are a selected group. Shapers with extreme pre-move profiles or outcomes may regress toward the mean, which could mimic or mask a profile effect.
Cut and drive shares and the portability score are noisy at small possession counts. The reliability of the role label is unknown.
Profile features must come from pre-move games only. Post-move or full-season data in the label would leak the outcome.
Many variants are possible (cut share, cut-drive, terciles, position splits, thresholds). Only one primary contrast should be allowed.
Role definitions and league play styles change across 2022-23 to 2025-26. Pooling seasons may mix regimes.

design.estimand: Spearman correlation between the pre-move cut-minus-drive share and the portability change score among shaper movers, with a bootstrap confidence interval. This is treated as a directional replication of FAM:SF-CHT-057. The cut-heavy vs drive-heavy contrast is a secondary descriptive comparison.
design.unit: One shaper mover (a player who changes team between consecutive observed seasons). If one player has several moves, use the earliest or random one, fixed in advance.
design.sample: The n=24 shaper movers in 2022-23 through 2025-26 (regular season plus playoffs where possession counts allow). Pre-specify the shaper definition and the minimum pre- and post-move possession thresholds before looking at outcomes. Report overlap with the 92 connector movers in FAM:SF-CHT-057 and do not pool the two. Treat 2025-26 moves as a holdout if the 2025-26 data are complete.
design.power: At n=24 and one-sided alpha=0.05, power for rho=0.27 to 0.31 is about 20-25%, and 80% power would need rho of about 0.55. State this in advance. Report estimates and intervals rather than only p-values. A null or inconclusive result will be labelled inconclusive, not rejected, unless the confidence interval excludes rho of about 0.25.
design.controls: Compute the profile from pre-move possessions only. Compute the portability outcome from post-move possessions and derive it so that it does not share the cut/drive inputs. Adjust for destination structural gap, usage or minutes change, and pre-move possession count, using a partial rank correlation or a small rank-based regression with at most 2-3 covariates given n. Report leave-one-out and drop-top-3 sensitivity.
design.falsification: Permute profile labels 5000 times as in FAM:SF-CHT-057. Run a placebo on a profile feature unrelated to the role (for example pre-move three-point share). Check that the effect does not appear in a pseudo-move pairing of non-movers across consecutive seasons. The hypothesis fails if the point estimate is zero or negative, or if the sign flips under leave-one-out.
design.multiplicity: One primary test (cut-minus-drive rho). The tercile comparison and the drive-only and cut-only shares are secondary and reported without claims. Holm correction applies if more than one is reported as confirmatory. No position splits.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if rho > 0 with the one-sided permutation p < 0.05, the bootstrap lower bound is above 0, and the sign holds in leave-one-out and in the holdout when available. Rejected only if the interval excludes rho of about 0.25 (unlikely at n=24). Otherwise inconclusive, and the best estimate of the effect is reported, not a verdict.
design.data_version: Per-game NBA stats API files and derived play-type possession records for 2022-23 through 2024-25 (regular season and playoffs), 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13) and 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21). Freeze the data snapshot and role definitions before analysis, and record the extraction date.

methodological_questions: How is role 'travel' or portability defined and measured when players change teams?
Is n=24 units enough power to compare cut-heavy and drive-heavy shapers?
How are shaper roles and cut-heavy/drive-heavy labels derived from play-by-play, and is the label outcome-derived?
How does regression to the mean or selection of movers affect role persistence estimates?
How do teammate and context changes confound role persistence across seasons?
args.query: Do cut-heavy shapers' roles persist or transfer across teams better than drive-heavy shapers' roles? Prior studies of role portability, role stability, shaper classification, and small-sample limits.

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)

Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=24

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

reasoning_details.text:
I'm going to write the final answer now, probably without any more tool calls. The question is whether cut-heavy shapers' roles travel better than drive-heavy ones, with n=24 units. The earlier finding from SF-CHT-057 was on connectors with n=92 movers and supported that cut share predicts portability, but I still need to check whether "shaper" and "connector" actually mean the same thing here.

I'm weighing whether the connector result carries over to shapers at n=24, since power at that size is low for the effect size seen before. Splitting into cut-heavy and drive-heavy groups would leave only about twelve per group. I'm leaning toward proceeding with a pre-specified, one-sided replication on the continuous cut-minus-drive measure, while expecting the result may be inconclusive.

I'm weighing the risks to this replication: the n=24 shaper sample is underpowered, the cut and drive shares come from the same play-type records as the portability measure, and the two shares are compositional, so their negative correlation is partly mechanical. Team confounds, selection of movers, and multiple testing also need attention, and I'm assigning rough odds to each outcome, with the testable share sitting near 30%.

Writing the design details concisely now.

The earlier finding from SF-CHT-057 was on connectors with n=92 movers and supported that cut share predicts portability, but I still need to check whether "shaper" and "connector" actually mean the same thing here.

I'm weighing whether the connector result carries over to shapers at n=24, since power at that size is low for the effect size seen before. Splitting into cut-heavy and drive-heavy groups would leave only about twelve per group. I'm leaning toward proceeding with a pre-specified, one-sided replication on the continuous cut-minus-drive measure, while expecting the result may be inconclusive.

I'm weighing the risks to this replication: the n=24 shaper sample is underpowered, the cut and drive shares come from the same play-type records as the portability measure, and the two shares are compositional, so their negative correlation is partly mechanical. Team confounds, selection of movers, and multiple testing also need attention, and I'm assigning rough odds to each outcome, with the testable share sitting near 30%.
